The migrated file is at `out/module.ts`. Type checking passes, and `npm run size -- out/module.ts` reports 606 bytes (min+gzip), with 95 bytes of your own code.

I couldn't run the same size command on the original `src/module.ts`. `lodash` isn't installed, so the build fails to resolve it, and I have no baseline to compare the 95 bytes against. I also didn't run a behaviour comparison against the original, for the same reason.

- **`keyBy`:** now comes from `es-toolkit`. It takes the same iteratee, so `byId` keeps its signature and returns the same keyed object.
- **`sumBy`:** now comes from `es-toolkit`. It only accepts a function, not lodash's `'age'` shorthand, so I changed the call to `(row) => row.age`. That is the only adapter.
- **`isEmpty`:** now comes from `es-toolkit/compat`. The main `es-toolkit` package has no equivalent. Its `isEmptyObject` only covers plain objects, so it would differ for numbers, booleans, strings and arrays. The compat version follows lodash's rules.
- **Smallest size:** I tried the compat versions of `keyBy` and `sumBy` as well. That build came to 3404 bytes, so I kept the main-package versions of those two. No `lodash` import remains.

The exports (`Row`, `Config`, `byId`, `totalAge`, `isBlank`) are unchanged.
